How to fill it in

Why a plain, single column

Most mid-size and large US employers use an applicant tracking system (ATS) to collect and search resumes. The software converts your file to text, and multi-column layouts, tables, text boxes, icons and images can come out jumbled. This template keeps everything in one flow with ordinary headings such as Experience, Skills and Education, so it reads the same to software and people.

Step 1: Contact line

Replace the name, headline, email, phone and location. City and state is enough; a full street address is not needed. Do not include a photo, age, marital status or Social Security number. Use a professional email address, and add a LinkedIn or portfolio link only if it is current.

Step 2: Write a short summary

Two or three sentences: your title, your years of experience, two real strengths and the job you want next. Skip the objective statement that says what you want from an employer; say what you offer instead. Keep it factual and specific.

Step 3: Write bullets that show results

For each recent job, write three to five bullets, and two or three for older roles. Use action verb + what you did + how + result. “Cut month-end close from eight days to five by automating bank reconciliations” is stronger than “Responsible for month-end close”. Add numbers where you honestly have them: dollars, percentages, volume, team size, time saved. Where you only have an estimate, say “about”. Where you have none, describe scope. Do not invent anything; interviewers ask.

Step 4: Tailor it to each posting

Read the job description and copy its key skills into your skills section and bullets only where it is true for you. Use the same words, such as “stakeholder reporting” or “Salesforce”, because ATS searches are often literal. Reorder bullets so the most relevant ones come first. Keep a master version with everything and trim for each application.

Step 5: Length and format

One page suits most people with under about ten years of experience; two pages are fine for more. Keep body text at 10 pt or above and cut the oldest content before shrinking type. Use consistent dates (Mar 2022 to Present) and US spelling. Submit a PDF unless the employer asks for Word, and name it Firstname-Lastname-Resume.pdf.

Final check

Paste the text from your PDF into a plain text editor. Is the order sensible? Are the email and phone intact? Then proofread for tense consistency and confirm every date, title and number.

Common mistakes to avoid

Five things cause most weak resumes. First, listing duties instead of results. Second, a skills section full of tools you have touched once. Third, inconsistent dates and tenses: use past tense for finished jobs and present tense only for your current one. Fourth, fancy formatting such as icons, skill bars and graphics, which add nothing an ATS can read. Fifth, sending the same resume to every job. A small amount of tailoring for each application, honestly done, is worth more than any design choice. Also keep the file name tidy and avoid sending a Word file with tracked changes or comments left inside.

Frequently asked questions

Is this resume template really free?

Yes. No email address or account is needed.

Is it ATS-friendly?

It is built to be: one column, standard headings, no tables, text boxes, images or icons. Systems differ, so test by copying the text out as described above.

Should I include a photo?

No. US employers generally do not expect one and it can create bias concerns.

Can I use Google Docs?

Yes, the .docx opens in Google Docs and Pages. Check spacing afterwards.

Is there a UK version?

Yes: the UK CV template uses A4 and UK spelling. There is also a two-column design.
